report.source_text: A punch biopsy of the nodule confirmed lobular panniculitis with an inflammatory cell infiltrate composed of numerous neutrophils, mixed with lymphocytes, eosinophils, histiocytes and occasional multinucleated giant cells (figure 2A). Granulomas were not observed. No features of vasculitis were identified. Gram-positive cocci were present in the dermis and subcutis (figure 2B). No fungal organisms or acid-fast bacilli were seen on Grocott’s methenamine silver or Ziehl-Neelsen stains. Culture from the punch biopsy grew MRSA.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A female in her 20s with relapsed Hodgkin lymphoma presented on day 11 of stem cell mobilization chemotherapy with fever (38.3°C) and bilateral tender, indurated subcutaneous nodules over the shins with mild erythema. Punch biopsy confirmed lobular panniculitis with neutrophilic infiltrate and gram-positive cocci in the dermis/subcutis; tissue culture grew MRSA. Blood cultures were negative, excluding bacteremia. Special stains ruled out fungal and mycobacterial organisms. She was treated with doxycycline, resulting in resolution of fever and nodules.
